title: introduce-budgeted-slimmer-engine-and-quant-tactician
author: Ravi Subramanian
release_notes: Add Budgeted Slimmer runtime module, tenant quant tactician and CLI simulator for unit-econ dry run; no breaking API changes
description: Context and motivation: We observed recurring tenant cost spikes caused by suboptimal batching shapes combined with overly conservative quant profiles. This PR introduces the Budgeted Slimmer engine which proactively trims batch shapes for tenants hitting budget thresholds and a Quant Tactician service that suggests tiered quantization profiles with safe rollback heuristics. The goal is to reduce per-token cost variability while preserving 99p latency SLOs. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/budgeted_slimmer: new adaptive batch-shape pruner with a safe backoff policy, 2) optimize/quant_tactician: recommendation engine that scores tenant workloads and proposes quant profiles per model family, 3) cli/econ_sim: a simulator to run deterministic dry-runs against historical traces and produce unit-econ delta reports, 4) telemetry: new econ.tactician and econ.slimmer metrics and dashboards, 5) tests: tenant-level integration tests and a smoke test in perf-canary. Rollout plan: gated feature flag redwood.econ.budgeted_slimmer default off, staged activation for 5 internal tenants then opt-in for customers; quant tactician suggestions are proposal-only until accepted by tenant policy. Checklist: - add feature flag and default off, - include unit tests and integration smoke tests, - add telemetry and dashboards, - implementation includes safe rollback and explicit audit logs. How to test locally: use cli/econ_sim with --trace sample_traces/tenant_small.json then inspect outputs in outputs/delta_report.json. Monitoring and safety: recommendations are recorded to audit log and include confidence score; the runtime will not apply aggressive trimming below configured latency floor and will immediately revert on latency regression detected by the canary alert rule. Docs: brief usage guide added to docs/ops/econ-automation.md. Related: builds on prior cost tooling work in ENG-3245 and addresses SUP-5021 incident mitigations.
